# SYNTHETIC machine (not a hardware capture): SPARSE NUMA node ids. Two
# CPU-bearing nodes numbered 0 and 4, with no nodes 1-3 -- node/online reads
# "0,4". Linux allows this (memory hotplug leaves gaps, and some ppc64 systems
# number nodes sparsely), which is why node/online is a list rather than a
# count.
#
# Node ids must pass through as the KERNEL's ids, not as indices into the
# enumerated set: an index would make "1" mean node 4, diverge from what
# numactl/lscpu report, make node 4 unreachable by name, and feed
# set_mempolicy a node that does not exist through the affinity group hint.
cpu/cpu0/cache/index0/level=1
cpu/cpu0/cache/index0/shared_cpu_list=0
cpu/cpu0/cache/index0/size=32K
cpu/cpu0/cache/index0/type=Data
cpu/cpu0/topology/core_cpus_list=0
cpu/cpu0/topology/core_id=0
cpu/cpu0/topology/physical_package_id=0
